messages:
sam: Heads-up — DCGM exporter on eu-west-gpu-pool spiked Xid/ECC counts overnight but it was concentrated to ~6 hosts. Flapping every ~15–30m, not a full node failure, but noisy alerts and a couple of automatic drains kicked in.

marta: Which metric mostly? ECC or Xid? Any correlation with MIG or multi-tenant pods?

sam: Mostly Xid on 3 hosts, ECC on 4 (one host had both). All cards are normal by eye after a reboot, errors drop to 0 then pop back later. No firmware or kernel upgrades during the window.

kevin: I captured the per-card series. This looks like short bursts, not sustained. I'm leaning toward smoothing/weighted-windowing + a quarantine tag instead of immediate node drain. Quick prototype PromQL I tested in staging:

kevin: ```
alert: NoisyGPUCardHighErrorRate
expr: |
  (
    increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[1m])*0.6 +
    increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m])*0.3 +
    increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[15m])*0.1
  ) +
  (
    increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1m])*0.6 +
    increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m])*0.3 +
    increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[15m])*0.1
  ) > 3
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  summary: "GPU card {{ $labels.instance }}/{{ $labels.gpu_index }} noisy (weighted window)"
  runbook: "https://redwood/internal/runbooks/gpu-noise"
```

kevin: This weights recent spikes heavier but still considers history. Stops a single transient spike from firing if it clears quickly.

lia: Nice. Can we also combine with a per-instance burst-counter so we suppress repeats from the same card for N minutes? Current alerts are stamping the pager on repeat.

sam: Yes — suggest adding a recording rule noisy_score and then a suppression rule that coalesces alerts per (instance,gpu_index) for 20m, with a decay factor so persistent problems still surface.

ops-bot: Automated suggestion: when noisy_score > 8 for > 30m, set k8s label gpu-quarantine=true on the node and reduce scheduling weight. Do not drain unless noisy_score > 20 or errors persist after 3 reboots.

devon: From a capacity POV, we should avoid full drains for transients — every drain moves work to other pools and increases burst capacity spend. Proposal: soft-quarantine (taint+lower-priority-pools) for 4h, if repeats over that period escalate to manual triage.

marta: Also saw these hosts were in the same rack. Could it be a PSU or PDU ripple causing transient Xid blips? Any network cards flapping at same times?

kevin: I checked NIC and switch logs — nothing obvious. But power telemetry shows slight correlated drops for two of the hosts (10s blips). Might be UPS switchover windows.

lia: Ops action: add a tag to those hosts (power-sensitive-rack=true) and target them for earlier firmware and power hardware sweeps. I'll open a vendor ticket.

sam: For Prometheus rule rollout plan:
- Create recording rule noisy_score in staging using the weighted expression (to make alert expr simpler).
- Add alert NoisyGPUCardHighErrorRate -> severity: warning, no immediate routing to pager (ops group only first).
- Add suppression: group_by(instance,gpu_index) with 20m coalesce.
- Add automated action in ops-bot: label/taint instead of drain for first bump.

kevin: Recording rule example (staging):
```
- record: gpu:noisy_score:sum
  expr: |
    sum by (instance,gpu_index)(
      (increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[1m])*0.6 + increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m])*0.3 + increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[15m])*0.1) +
      (increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1m])*0.6 + increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m])*0.3 + increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[15m])*0.1)
    )
```

lia: We should also emit a metric for "time_since_last_error" per gpu_index so we can escalate if errors reappear within short intervals. That helps detect flappers vs one-offs.

devon: Cost note: If we go soft-quarantine + hold-off, expected utilization dip of ~2–3% for the pool during incidents which is OK vs full drains that cause cross-region shifts. Will model in cost dashboard once we have historical counts.

marta: Test cases to validate:
- Single 30s spike should not page.
- Repeating spikes every 20m for 3 hours should escalate to manual triage.
- Simulate power blip correlated across rack to verify we don't mislabel node hardware as card-failures.

sam: I'll open a small RFC and add the prometheus PR for staging rules. If folks agree, I'll push to canary next week (non-pager), and we'll collect data for 2 weeks.

kevin: Also adding Grafana panel for gpu:noisy_score by rack to catch rack-level events early.

ops-bot: Action created: TICKET-1224 "Investigate eu-west rack power blips + implement weighted DCGM noise rule" assigned to lia, kevin, sam.

lia: Thanks — I'll start vendor engagement and tag the hosts.

sam: Cool. If anyone sees a true hardware pattern (constant high ECC/Xid > 100/hr), please escalate and mark for replacement. For these flappers let's try smoothing + quarantine first. :thumbsup:
